web_evidence.title: The Appeal by John Grisham
web_evidence.note: Author-hosted Chapter One excerpt narrates the jury's collective feelings and the bailiff's actions externally. Establishes the opening only.

web_evidence.title: The Appeal — publisher sample
web_evidence.note: Publisher sample includes Chapters 1–2. Inspected passages move from Trudeau and Ratzlaff to Jeannette, reporting actions and private thoughts through nonparticipating narration. Chapter 2's first-person plural passage is explicitly Jeannette speaking to herself, not a new base narrator.

web_evidence.title: Third Person Point of View Types Explained
web_evidence.note: Writing-craft article explicitly classifies The Appeal as distant third person and illustrates its claim with a Trudeau scene. Its illustration is local, so this is corroboration rather than exhaustive structural proof.

person_note: A nonparticipating narrator reports multiple characters' actions and thoughts. Diagnostic Goodreads passages independently agree with authorized prose across two chapters and an explicit third-person description. Generic 'you', dialogue, and Jeannette's locally attributed 'we' thoughts do not establish alternate base narration. The remaining limitation is that the authorized sample does not cover the entire novel; no credible contradictory structure was found.
